deed: שלושה ישראלים רשמו פטנט על כונן ה-USB — והעולם עדיין מתווכח מי המציא
title: Amir Ban, Dov Moran and Oron Ogdan of M-Systems patented the USB flash drive

trailer.text: Dov Moran is an Israeli electrical engineer and businessman, known mainly as the inventor of the USB drive.
In 1989 Moran founded the Israeli company M-Systems, which worked in flash memory storage devices.
In April 1999 M-Systems filed a patent application for a "flash disk" for a personal computer that connects via USB.
The patent was granted to Amir Ban, Dov Moran and Oron Ogdan in November 2000.
That same year IBM began selling M-Systems' device, with a capacity of 8 megabytes, in the United States under the name DiskOnKey.

glance.label: Inventors
glance.value: M-Systems' patent on the USB-based flash drive was granted to Amir Ban, Dov Moran and Oron Ogdan in November 2000.

glance.label: Product
glance.value: DiskOnKey, 8 megabytes, sold by IBM from 2000

glance.label: The market today
glance.value: In 2021, global sales of USB drives from all manufacturers surpassed $7 billion, and according to the forecast they will exceed $10 billion by 2028.

paragraphs.text: Before the USB flash drive, most users relied on floppy disks.
The common floppy disk held 1.44 megabytes.
A large file had to be split across many floppy disks.
Another option was a high-density disk.
Such a disk required special, expensive and sometimes unreliable hardware.
According to IEEE Spectrum, computer users badly needed a portable, cheap, reliable, high-capacity storage device.
According to Britannica, in the late 1990s industry experts saw pairing USB with flash memory as the obvious next step.
In the Navy he was commander of the microprocessor section.
He was its CEO and chairman.
According to the patent, flash devices have an advantage: they are relatively inexpensive and use little power compared with magnetic disks.
According to the patent, they also have a limitation that makes them incompatible with the programs of existing operating systems.
On 5 April 1999 M-Systems filed the patent application.
The application was titled Architecture for a universal serial bus-based PC flash disk.
Ban, Moran and Ogdan assigned the patent to M-Systems Flash Disk Pioneers.
In November 2000 the patent, number 6,148,354, was granted.
In March 2000 a European application was also filed, by M-Systems Flash Disk Pioneers and Milsys.
According to the patent, the invention is a flash memory device in which the memory is connected to a controller with a USB interface.
The USB controller receives data packets from the bus.
According to them, it writes data to the memory and reads data from it.
According to the European patent, an address resolve module translates the address from the logical space to the physical space.
According to the patent, the entire device acts as a drive that retains data even without power.
It can be connected to and disconnected from the computer at any moment.
In the example in the patent, the device has two flash modules.
Each module is 64 megabits in size.
M-Systems' product was called DiskOnKey.
A team led by Dan Harkabi developed it.
It was announced in September 2000.
In 2000 IBM began selling the device, with a capacity of 8 megabytes, in the United States.
This was more than five times the capacity of the then-common floppy disk.
In 2006 the company was sold to SanDisk.
In 2008 the name of the patent holder was changed to SanDisk IL Ltd.
USB flash drives are usually smaller and faster than floppy disks and CD-ROMs.
They are also more reliable and durable, because they have no moving parts.
In 2004, 1GB drives reached the market.
By 2010 they had been replaced by 128GB models.
According to IEEE Spectrum, the USB flash drive effectively ended the era of the floppy disk.
In 2021 global sales of USB flash drives, from all manufacturers, passed $7 billion.
Even after the move to cloud services, USB flash drives remain popular.
According to StorageNewsletter, the M-Systems patent describes a product that has a cable between the memory unit and the USB connector.
According to IEEE Spectrum, IBM claims credit for an aspect of the device.
It relies on a confidential internal report written by employee Shimon Shmueli.
According to Britannica, IBM sent an invention disclosure by Shmueli to the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office in the same year that M-Systems filed the patent.
In 2000, the Singapore company Trek 2000 presented, at a trade fair in Germany, a memory chip encased in plastic and attached to a USB connector.
The device held 8 megabytes and required no external power source.
Trek, led by Henn Tan, filed a Singapore patent application on 21 February 2000, about a week before the German technology fair where it introduced the device.
Between April and July 2000 Trek manufactured and sold more than 100,000 ThumbDrives.
Trek won a lawsuit in Singapore.
It persuaded the judge that the ThumbDrive was the first device designed to plug directly into a computer without a cable.
In the United Kingdom the argument failed: in 2006 the UK Patent Office revoked Trek's patent, and in 2008 the High Court dismissed its appeal.
According to IEEE Spectrum, after auditors revealed acts of falsification in 2015, Tan stepped down.
In August 2022 he pled guilty to falsifying accounts.
According to StorageNewsletter, most manufacturers make USB flash drives without regard for the patents of Trek and Netac.

disagreements.question: Who invented the USB flash drive, and who was first?

versions.says: According to StorageNewsletter, Ban, Moran and Ogdan of M-Systems invented the drive and filed the patent in April 1999
According to StorageNewsletter, IBM's invention disclosure of 13 September 1999, by Shimon Shmueli, accurately describes the USB flash drive
According to Britannica, Trek 2000 of Singapore was the first to actually sell a USB flash drive, called ThumbDrive
According to StorageNewsletter, Trek and Netac claimed credit based on patents later than that of M-Systems
Cheng Xiaohua and Deng Guoshun had previously worked at Trek and founded Netac in 1999, and Netac received a patent on the drive in China
According to Britannica, Netac's claim is difficult to prove for its drive, U Disk, which appeared on the market only in 2002
According to StorageNewsletter, Pua Khein-Seng of Malaysia claims to have incorporated the world's first USB controller on a single chip
According to IEEE Spectrum, inventors in Malaysia and China claimed to have been first, but less credibly
According to Britannica, it is highly likely that most of the claimants developed their own USB flash drives independently

disagreements.question: Who was first on the market?

versions.says: According to Britannica, Trek 2000 was the first to actually sell a USB flash drive
According to StorageNewsletter, in 2000 both Trek, with ThumbDrive, and IBM, with M-Systems' DiskOnKey, introduced USB flash drives to the market
